rationale: Both candidates independently found the same real host-device-sync hot-path issue and the unsupported 'within 2%' doc claim, but neither found GT's P2 concern (aligned-input duplicate boundary silently disabling SAGE) — X even mis-marks that exact code path as '[resolved]', a false negative. On GT's P1 concern (AllGather-KV breaking packed metadata), X's finding mislabels a likely pre-existing guard as 'added by this diff' and rates it 'minor', while Y correctly frames it as pre-existing/name-based and pinpoints the real root cause (unhonored query_ranges), closely matching bobboli's actual diagnosis. Y also surfaces two novel, well-grounded correctness bugs (all-False mask launching a zero-token kernel; unvalidated max_seqlen_q/k) with concrete repros and code-level fixes, plus engages the timestep/sigma follow-up via a test-gap analysis, giving it broader recall and slightly higher precision/actionability than X's still-solid but narrower review.
